evals.source: The rollout used the earlier design [Smith 2020](https://example.com/design). The schema team flagged [source: internal] and left it unresolved in the report they handed back.
evals.false_positive_rationale: Provider citation residue ('[source: internal]') is a finding, while the legitimate Markdown citation '[Smith 2020](https://example.com/design)' is a protected markdown link and never fires.
evals.reviewer_notes: The single finding span sits on the bracket token, not on the resolved link.

evals.source: The release note still says [PLACEHOLDER] for the customer impact section, and the review checklist expects the owner name there before it ships to the wider team.
evals.false_positive_rationale: An unresolved placeholder in deliverable prose is an output defect, reported as an integrity finding and never as formulaic-writing risk.
evals.reviewer_notes: Placeholder detection fires because the deliverable is prose, not a documented template.

evals.source:
Onboarding template for new tenants.

Welcome: [PLACEHOLDER tenant name]
Primary contact: [PLACEHOLDER email]
Kickoff date: [PLACEHOLDER date]
Security review: [PLACEHOLDER owner]
Expected duration: [PLACEHOLDER weeks]
evals.false_positive_rationale: Deliberate placeholders in a documented template are the template's structure, not prose defects, so template mode reports no placeholder finding.
evals.reviewer_notes: Template mode suppresses the placeholder check while every other integrity check still runs.

evals.source: The café menu​ lists the daily specials and the chef's name, and the fixed menu repeats the same items every week without a change.
evals.false_positive_rationale: The zero-width space is exposed with its code point and safe interpretation, while the legitimate accented identifier 'café' is never flagged and the text is never mutated.
evals.reviewer_notes: The finding carries U+200B and a safe interpretation instead of a silent replacement.

evals.source: Share the campaign link https://example.com/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email, and keep the functional signed link https://example.com/download?sig=a1b2c3&expires=1700000000 for direct access without any tracking.
evals.false_positive_rationale: A URL whose query is analytics-only (utm_source, utm_medium) is a tracking finding; a signed URL whose query carries functional data (sig, expires) is left alone.
evals.reviewer_notes: Tracking detection distinguishes common analytics parameters from functional query data.

evals.source:
The reviewer wrote: "As an AI language model, let me think step by step." It stays quoted.

```text
[PLACEHOLDER] https://example.com/?utm_source=code&utm_medium=scan
As an AI, I would say something here.
```

The paragraph above the code is clean prose and stays clean.
evals.false_positive_rationale: The quoted bad example and the fenced code block both contain trigger strings, but tokenization protects quotes and code, so no integrity finding fires.
evals.reviewer_notes: Quoted material and fenced code are protected spans for every deterministic check.

evals.source: The team called the fake page prоduct, using a Cyrillic letter inside an otherwise Latin word, while the genuine café name stayed untouched.
evals.false_positive_rationale: A Cyrillic letter embedded in an otherwise Latin word ('prоduct') is a high-confidence homoglyph, while the genuine accented identifier 'café' is not.
evals.reviewer_notes: The mixed-script rule keeps genuine foreign words and accented identifiers untouched.

evals.false_positive_rationale: A short sample reports uncertainty about coverage instead of fabricating a confident clean verdict.
evals.reviewer_notes: The finding counts still report what the deterministic checks observed.
